the serum of patients with IBD does not suppress the suppressor cell function of peripheral blood mononucleocytes (PBMCs).

the role of the suppressor T-cell in the pathogenesis of IBD.
the regulation of the immune system and the role of suppressor T cells in inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis).
the regulation of suppressor cell activity by serum factors in inflammatory disorders.

the pathogenesis of IBD has not been elucidated and that the disease is multifactorial in origin.
the pathogenesis of IBD is not known, and the evidence is insufficient to support the hypothesis that IBD is an immunological disease.

the serum of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s and ulcerative colitis) does not contain a factor that inhibits suppressor cell function.
